index.name: Topics in Software Engineering: AI in SE

header.name: Topics in Software Engineering: AI in SE
header.offered_to: MTech, PhD students, BTech students with permission based on evaluation of their background, preparation, and motivation.
header.description:
Modern methods of engineering software generate a lot of data – almost all artifacts produced in a software project are machine processable, projects capture a lot of data in various repositories like source code control, bug tracking, etc., programmers’ activities log is available, companies have project database with data on past projects, proposals submitted, etc. 
 
 Using data for SE has been around for quite some time (e.g. Mining Software Repositories is an area that focuses on getting knowledge from the data.) However, over the last decade AI techniques have really matured, and AI models are being applied in SE much more – e.g. by automating more tasks, monitoring project health, providing assistance to engineers or managers, providing guidance for decisions, etc. Besides using AI for the activities helping projects or engineers, AI techniques can also be used by companies which execute hundreds of projects, to benefit from better monitoring and control of their portfolio of projects, better utilization and planning of resources, better risk management, etc. The use of AI in SE is an emerging area with a lot of promise and activity.
 
 The goal of this course is to introduce various research challenges and state of the art in applying AI for SE issues. Each week will cover one topic. Students are expected to take active part in discussions. Topics will be discussed in conjunction with various seminal papers related to that topic. Some of the lectures on various topics will be given by the instructor and some invited experts. Student groups will also give lectures on various topics.
 
 The course is being offered by multiple institutes parallelly. As a result, faculty from multiple institutes will be teaching the course and students from multiple institutes will be attending the course. 
 
 The course will also be offered to a limited number participants from industry (they can join as casual students – provision for it is there) – this will not only enhance the discussions in the class, but also help these companies in applying AI.

prerequisites.raw: Knowledge of AI and Learning techniques and familiarity with Software Engineering
Knowledge of Software Engineering and familiarity with AI/ML

cos.label: CO1
cos.text: Familiarity about how AI is being used for addressing different problems in SE

cos.label: CO2
cos.text: In-depth understanding of use of AI models in one particular SE issue

cos.label: CO3
cos.text: Understanding of how to apply AI models for a different domain (SE in this case)

cos.label: CO4
cos.text: Improved ability to review research literature and understand the state of the art in some area

cos.label: CO5
cos.text: Improved ability to do independent research

lecture_weeks.topic_raw: · Performance (software or system) tuning or prediction
· Assisting code review and code analysis
· Project management (various aspects like estimation, risk management, …)
· Improving the monitoring of health of a project
· Analyzing logs and user comments (for bug detection, issues, etc.)

assessment.raw_label: Students will form small groups and will take up specific topics. They will give a lecture on the state of the art in the selected topic, and write a short report. They will also try to formulate a R&D problem in that topic for applying ML in the chosen SE-problem, and research plan for addressing it, and do some work on the problem (they can later expand this as IP/IS/UR/ Thesis…). For each lecture, some topic and papers will be assigned for reading, which the students are expected to read, and actively participate in the discussions. The elements of evaluation and their rough weights are:
State of art Report on the chosen topic
Research in the chosen topic - R&D problem formulation and some work
